newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Uninspired Singapore shares end almost unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Uninspired Singapore shares end almost unchanged.

text.p: Singapore shares were almost unchanged on Tuesday after a trading day which lacked inspiration, dealers said.
"Things on the whole are very quiet," said a dealer at a local firm after a session in which a moderate 152 million shares changed hands, producing 259 losers and 94 gainers.
Currency concerns were still lingering and the attendant fears of instability gave investors "little incentive to get into the market now", another dealer said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index reflected the lack of commitment ending the day barely changed at 1,977.10, up 2.09.
Only confirmation that electronics manufacturing would lead the Singapore economy back onto an upward track could provide any impetus, one dealer said.
"Everything hangs on electronics, but we need more conclusive economic numbers before we are certain (of recovery)," he said.
However, the two most-watched electronics stocks of recent trading sessions failed to delight on Tuesday.

Creative Technology gained Singapore $0.10 to S$34.00 after announcing profits of US$167 million in line with expectations, and competitor Venture fell S$0.40 to S$6.50 after two days of heavy gains following a product launch.
Malaysia's Berjaya Land led the day's gaining issues, up S$0.50 to S$3.74. UOB Bank foreign shares led losers, down S$0.70 to S$15.80.
